chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Mismā‘ Abu Sayyar, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: “That Amir al-Mu’minin عليه السلام was brought a pickpocket who had stealthily taken dirhams from a man’s cloak, so he said:”
“If he had cut it out from his upper shirt, we would not amputate him; but if he had cut it out from his lower shirt, we would amputate him.”

key_terms.طَرَّ: secretly slit or cut and took from a garment, referring here to pickpocketing
key_terms.قَمِيصِهِ الْأَعْلَى: his upper garment or outer shirt

ai.seo_question: When does amputation apply in a case of pickpocketing according to this hadith from Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Amir al-Mu’minin عليه السلام concerning theft by pickpocketing. It distinguishes between taking from an outer garment and taking from an inner garment, indicating a juridical difference in when the hadd punishment of amputation applies.
